# nestarc

> Open-source NestJS reliability building blocks for multi-tenant SaaS backends.

Canonical site: https://nestarc.dev/
Organization: https://nestarc.dev/about
GitHub: https://github.com/nestarc
npm: https://www.npmjs.com/org/nestarc

## Start here

- https://nestarc.dev/getting-started
- https://nestarc.dev/packages/
- https://nestarc.dev/guide/
- https://nestarc.dev/api/
- https://nestarc.dev/blog/
- https://nestarc.dev/faq

## @nestarc/tenancy 0.16.1

Confirm the installed package version and peer dependencies before applying an example. This guide describes tenancy 0.16.1 with Node.js ^22.13.0 || ^24.0.0, NestJS 10/11, and Prisma 6/7.

- Agent usage guide: https://nestarc.dev/packages/tenancy/agent-guide
- Installation and role/RLS prerequisites: https://nestarc.dev/packages/tenancy/installation
- Authentication and identifier extraction: https://nestarc.dev/packages/tenancy/extractors
- Public API and subpaths: https://nestarc.dev/api/tenancy/modules
- Migration: https://nestarc.dev/packages/tenancy/migration
- CLI check and JSON doctor: https://nestarc.dev/packages/tenancy/cli
- Runnable source example: https://github.com/nestarc/nestjs-tenancy/tree/v0.16.1/examples/quickstart

Headers and decoded JWT claims do not authorize tenant access. Authenticate before extraction, authorize membership, use a restricted non-owner database role, and apply RLS policies. Raw SQL requires explicit transaction-local context. Repository main can contain changes not yet published to npm; compare its version and release notes with the installed package.

## @nestarc/audit-log 0.8.0

Confirm the installed version with `npm ls @nestarc/audit-log`. These guides cover published 0.8.0 with Node.js ^22.23.4 || ^24.22.1, NestJS 10/11/12.0.1+, and Prisma 5/6/7 peers. PostgreSQL is the default provider. SQL Server supports explicit manual logging and tenant-scoped history queries; its pinned validation stack is SQL Server 2025 with Prisma CLI/client/MSSQL adapter 7.10.0. On PostgreSQL, Prisma 7 uses the generated client namespace and PostgreSQL adapter; existing Prisma 5/6 client construction can remain in place.

- Run the pinned example and verify the first role change: https://nestarc.dev/packages/audit-log/quickstart
- Adopt one manual business event or one tracked model: https://nestarc.dev/packages/audit-log/adoption
- Agent usage guide: https://nestarc.dev/packages/audit-log/agent-guide
- Shared configuration, schema, and module installation: https://nestarc.dev/packages/audit-log/installation
- Automatic tracking boundaries: https://nestarc.dev/packages/audit-log/auto-tracking
- Manual events, managed/caller-owned transactions, validation and diagnostics: https://nestarc.dev/packages/audit-log/manual-logging
- Authorized history queries: https://nestarc.dev/packages/audit-log/query-api
- SQL Server setup, permissions and provider limits: https://nestarc.dev/packages/audit-log/sql-server
- Upgrade to 0.8.0: https://nestarc.dev/packages/audit-log/migration
- Published public API: https://nestarc.dev/api/audit-log/
- Version-pinned release source: https://github.com/nestarc/nestjs-audit-log/blob/v0.8.0/CHANGELOG.md

Start with one role change and verify actor, authorized tenant, before/after values, masking, and rollback. A manual user.role.changed event records application-supplied values in metadata.role; an automatic User.updated record uses changes.role. Manual adoption needs only the module and table. withManualTransaction(base, async ({ tx, log }) => ...) owns a new transaction; use tx for business writes and await the bound log(input). Caught audit failures still prevent commit, started writes settle before completion, and expired writers reject. For a caller-owned transaction, keep log(input, tx) and propagate audit failures. Automatic adoption uses trackedModels: ['User'] and withAuditTransaction(); caught atomic audit/policy errors still prevent commit.

defineAuditConfig() builds module, optional extension, schema, and partition options without database work or Nest registration. actorRequired defaults to false; enabling it requires a non-blank string ID for system actors too. Use actorExtractionStage: 'interceptor' after authentication Guards; middleware remains the default. Actor extraction and tenant audit context do not authenticate, authorize, or scope business queries. Use trusted tenant context and tenant predicates in business queries.

strictManualValidation defaults to false and validates manual event/metadata inputs when enabled. maxMetadataBytes is an independent positive UTF-8 byte budget for the final redacted JSON; oversized inputs reject before INSERT without truncation. AuditInputError exposes code and field without input values. onAuditOperation observes outcomes/durations without event contents and isolates observer failures; a successful log outcome means INSERT completed, not transaction commit. getCapabilities() reports configured provider API support without verifying the live schema or privileges.

SQL Server query()/getById() require authorized tenant scope and a reader with SELECT privileges. Exact text filters distinguish case, accents, and trailing spaces; opaque cursors preserve DATETIME2(7) precision. Optional read indexes are an explicit schema operation. SQL Server automatic tracking, scan/export, retention, partitioning, GIN indexes, and rule enforcement remain unsupported.

Atomic tracked createMany, updateMany, createManyAndReturn, and updateManyAndReturn are rejected before mutation; returning-bulk rejection is a breaking change in 0.7.0. Use sequential supported writes inside the helper. deleteMany has a per-record cap. Nested writes to tracked models are rejected even through untracked parents. Base clients, raw SQL, database cascades, and intentional exclusions are not automatically audited. best-effort is non-atomic; returning bulk APIs produce no automatic rows. Soft-delete 0.7.4 excludes audit-log 0.8.0 in its peer range. The separate lifecycle recipes remain pinned to audit-log 0.7.0 / soft-delete 0.7.4; do not substitute 0.8.0 or bypass peer validation. A newer combined tuple requires a compatible published companion and passing strict-peer lifecycle checks.

## @nestarc/feature-flag 0.6.0

Confirm the installed version with `npm ls @nestarc/feature-flag`. These guides cover published 0.6.0 with NestJS 10/11, the required @prisma/client ^7 peer, and Node.js ^20.19.0 || ^22.12.0 || >=24.0.0. Custom repositories can replace the default Prisma-backed repository, and tenantContextProvider can be passed to forRoot/forRootAsync; the package's peer requirements still apply. No database migration is required from 0.5.

- Agent guide and upgrade boundary: https://nestarc.dev/packages/feature-flag/agent-guide
- Installation and first HTTP result: https://nestarc.dev/packages/feature-flag/installation
- Evaluation and bucketing: https://nestarc.dev/packages/feature-flag/rollout
- Attribute overrides: https://nestarc.dev/packages/feature-flag/tenant-overrides
- Cache consistency: https://nestarc.dev/packages/feature-flag/cache-adapters
- Custom providers: https://nestarc.dev/packages/feature-flag/custom-backends
- Published API: https://nestarc.dev/api/feature-flag/modules
- Release source: https://github.com/nestarc/nestjs-feature-flag/blob/v0.6.0/CHANGELOG.md

Explicit targetingKey and registry bucketBy are now applied consistently, including typed/bulk evaluation; invocation/Admin bucketBy is available. Review partial-rollout cohorts when upgrading because decisions may change. Module options configure providers; tokens only in an importing module do not replace internal providers. Redis invalidation remains best-effort. evaluateAll returns active stored flags, propagates errors, and does not substitute registry defaults or emit per-flag exposure events. OpenFeature supports Boolean flags only and its public types require @openfeature/server-sdk ^1.23.0.

## @nestarc/webhook 0.13.2

Confirm the installed version and peer dependencies. Published webhook 0.13.2 supports NestJS 10/11 and Prisma 5/6/7; Prisma 7 needs a generated client and PostgreSQL adapter. Select a Node.js runtime compatible with all chosen dependencies.

- Agent guide: https://nestarc.dev/packages/webhook/agent-guide
- Installation and first delivery: https://nestarc.dev/packages/webhook/installation
- Publishing and tenant scope: https://nestarc.dev/packages/webhook/sending-events
- Attempts, retries, and replay: https://nestarc.dev/packages/webhook/delivery-logs
- Signatures and receiver deduplication: https://nestarc.dev/packages/webhook/security
- Published API: https://nestarc.dev/api/webhook/
- Korean introduction: https://nestarc.dev/ko/packages/webhook/
- Release source: https://github.com/nestarc/webhook/blob/v0.13.2/CHANGELOG.md

send() matches endpoints across all tenants; use sendToTenant() for tenant events. Receivers need persistent webhook-id deduplication as well as raw-body HMAC and timestamp checks. Keys are snapshotted at delivery creation. Version 0.13.2 persists correlationId without idempotencyKey, uses the configured total attempt budget for replay, and coordinates retry/replay with payload purge under event-row locks. Custom repositories must honor the optional correlation metadata and replay budget. Administrative reason remains unpersisted in the built-in Prisma adapter. A delivery acknowledgement does not prove exactly-once downstream effects.

## @nestarc/outbox 0.4.0

Confirm the installed version with `npm ls @nestarc/outbox`. These guides cover published 0.4.0 with Node.js >=22, NestJS 10/11/12, Prisma 5/6/7, and PostgreSQL. Pair NestJS 12 with Schedule 12; Prisma 7's PostgreSQL adapter needs pg even when wakeups are disabled.

- Agent guide: https://nestarc.dev/packages/outbox/agent-guide
- SQL, providers, upgrade, and shutdown: https://nestarc.dev/packages/outbox/installation
- Delivery, claims, retries, and cursors: https://nestarc.dev/packages/outbox/how-it-works
- Publisher adapters: https://nestarc.dev/packages/outbox/transports
- Published API: https://nestarc.dev/api/outbox/
- Korean introduction: https://nestarc.dev/ko/packages/outbox/
- Release source: https://github.com/nestarc/outbox/blob/v0.4.0/CHANGELOG.md

Keep polling enabled: polling.enabled:false now fails initialization even with LISTEN/NOTIFY. Version 2 listPage cursors preserve PostgreSQL microseconds; restart old traversals because v1 cursors are rejected. Current 0.3 schemas need no additional SQL migration. Enable Nest shutdown hooks; the poller drains for at most 30 seconds. Preserve message IDs and deduplicate side effects. SENT is acknowledgement, not downstream completion or FIFO. Jobs 0.4.0 declares Outbox ^0.2.1 || ^0.3.0, so the site's combined jobs workflow intentionally pins Outbox 0.3.0; do not substitute 0.4.0 into that recipe without a compatible bridge and verified package tuple.

## @nestarc/data-subject 0.3.0

Confirm the installed version with `npm ls @nestarc/data-subject`. These guides cover published 0.3.0, which includes breaking changes from 0.2.0. The package declares Node.js >=20, NestJS ^10.0.0 || ^11.2.7, and optional Prisma ^5.0.0 || ^7.10.0. Prisma 6 is outside the peer range; the selected framework and Prisma versions may require a newer Node.js runtime.

- Introduction and persistent request schema: https://nestarc.dev/packages/data-subject/
- Installation and shared definitions: https://nestarc.dev/packages/data-subject/installation
- Upgrade from 0.2.0: https://nestarc.dev/packages/data-subject/migration
- Policy and export allowlists: https://nestarc.dev/packages/data-subject/policy-model
- Export, erasure, and evidence: https://nestarc.dev/packages/data-subject/export-erase
- Transaction and lifecycle hooks: https://nestarc.dev/packages/data-subject/events-hooks
- Signed previews, durable recovery, and paged jobs: https://nestarc.dev/packages/data-subject/execution
- Published public API: https://nestarc.dev/api/data-subject/modules
- Version-pinned host example: https://github.com/nestarc/data-subject/tree/v0.3.0/examples/tenant-safe
- Version-pinned release source: https://github.com/nestarc/data-subject/blob/v0.3.0/CHANGELOG.md

Use explicit exportFields; omitted or empty allowlists exclude the entity, and allowlisted objects include their nested values. Authenticate, authorize, and verify the subject before calling the service. Tenant-scoped lookups still need a subject/owner check in the host. Stable scalar identity and selectByIds verification are required for erasure by default. Prefer definePolicy() definitions shared with lint.

Immediate execution does not guarantee rollback. Signed previews require transaction-bound executors and Serializable isolation; durable execution needs its own model/migration and transaction binding. Artifact or notification failure does not mean data erasure rolled back. Use lifecycle metadata and original-byte recovery instead of blindly repeating erase. Optional paged jobs commit each page separately, so cancellation or failure can leave earlier pages committed. In-memory stores are for local use; private artifact storage, authorization, and retention remain application responsibilities. The package does not confer legal compliance.

## @nestarc/safe-response 0.16.0

Use published 0.16.0 with the declared NestJS 10/11 and Swagger 8/11 peer lines; check the selected framework's Node requirements. The /client entrypoint supplies framework-independent response types and guards.

- Installation and compatibility: https://nestarc.dev/packages/safe-response/installation
- Payload and client contracts: https://nestarc.dev/packages/safe-response/response-format
- Error codes: https://nestarc.dev/packages/safe-response/error-codes
- API deprecation: https://nestarc.dev/packages/safe-response/response-format#api-deprecation
- Swagger contracts: https://nestarc.dev/packages/safe-response/swagger
- Published API: https://nestarc.dev/api/safe-response/modules
- Release source: https://github.com/nestarc/nestjs-safe-response/blob/v0.16.0/CHANGELOG.md

Only success types admitting undefined can omit data; SafeSuccessResponse is a conditional type alias, so use intersections instead of interface extension/declaration merging. Express payload limits return 413/PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE. Deprecation fallback uses RFC 9745 date syntax. Field selection is immutable, parent selection includes its whole value, and repeated cursor filters survive navigation. Response envelopes use the handler's final status. Keep concrete DTO and pagination schema constraints; untyped payload schemas allow primitives, arrays, and null.

## @nestarc/soft-delete 0.7.4

The published 0.7.4 peer range adds audit-log ^0.7.0 after 0.7.3 added ^0.6.0; runtime and schema behavior are unchanged from 0.7.2. The version-pinned lifecycle recipes pair audit-log 0.7.0 with soft-delete 0.7.4. Audit-log 0.8.0 is excluded by that peer range; do not substitute it or bypass peer validation. Use the Node/Nest/Prisma intersection of all installed companions.

- Installation and peers: https://nestarc.dev/packages/soft-delete/installation
- Atomic lifecycle and events: https://nestarc.dev/packages/soft-delete/events
- Restore and purge: https://nestarc.dev/packages/soft-delete/restore-purge
- Extension composition: https://nestarc.dev/guide/prisma-extension-chaining
- Published API: https://nestarc.dev/api/soft-delete/modules
- Release manifest: https://github.com/nestarc/nestjs-soft-delete/blob/v0.7.4/package.json

Atomic lifecycle setup still requires the capability handshake, tenancy → audit-log → soft-delete order, and withAuditTransaction(). Repository dev pins are historical verification evidence, not proof that every permitted companion tuple was exercised. The pinned audit-log 0.7.0/soft-delete 0.7.4 recipe declares Node ^22.13.0 || ^24.0.0 and shares NestJS 10/11; use a patched runtime. Standalone audit-log 0.8.0 requires Node ^22.23.4 || ^24.22.1.

## @nestarc/idempotency 1.0.0

Published 1.0.0 requires Node.js 22 or 24 and NestJS 10/11. Import RedisStorage from @nestarc/idempotency/redis and PostgreSQL storage/sweep APIs from @nestarc/idempotency/postgres. Install optional drivers explicitly; PostgreSQL TypeScript consumers also install @types/pg. Root memory-only imports do not require those drivers.

- Installation: https://nestarc.dev/packages/idempotency/installation
- Coordinated migration and rollback: https://nestarc.dev/packages/idempotency/migration
- HTTP and failure semantics: https://nestarc.dev/packages/idempotency/how-it-works
- Storage adapters and ownership: https://nestarc.dev/packages/idempotency/storage
- Public import paths: https://nestarc.dev/api/idempotency/modules
- Release source: https://github.com/nestarc/idempotency/blob/v1.0.0/CHANGELOG.md

Move 0.x installations to a separate empty namespace and stop old/new process overlap in both upgrade and rollback. Hashed keys have no legacy fallback; opaque response bodies must be stored unchanged. A namespace switch cannot prevent historical business duplicates: preserve durable business deduplication and reconcile past retries. Custom scope identities augment endpoint isolation. Unsupported response capture retains its processing lease; expiry or ambiguous storage writes still need business reconciliation. Register idempotency before response transformers. Telemetry exposes hashed namespace/keyHash and fixed error classifications; hashes are not anonymity guarantees or metric labels.

## Notes for automated clients

- Package compatibility and limitations are documented on each package page.
- Technical articles include reviewed dates and version scopes.
- Generated API references describe the current documented releases.
- This file is a convenience index, not a ranking or citation signal.
